diagnostic_evidence.quote: Additionally, other choices of $\delta$ might lead to even (slightly) weaker conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side of the condition (cond_prop31), ((δ-1)/(δBTE))^{1/β}, equals ((δ-1)/δ)^{1/β}(BTE)^{-1/β}; comparing δ=8 to δ=2 yields the improvement factor ((7/8)/(1/2))^{1/β} = (7/4)^{1/β}, which is strictly less than 7^{1/β}, not at least 7^{1/β}. Moreover, the induced bound on AE, δ^{-1-1/β}(δ-1)^{1/β}(BTE)^{-1/β}, is maximized at δ = β+1, so for the paper's own application β=2 the choice δ=8 is strictly worse than δ=2. The claimed improvement is therefore false.

failure_location.quote: Secondly, choosing $\delta = 8$, we see that we improved the upper bound of the condition at least by a factor of $7^{1/\beta}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the factor in the remark (the δ=8 versus δ=2 improvement is (7/4)^{1/β}, and the optimal choice is δ = β+1) or delete the quantitative comparison.
issues.overall_effect: Only the comparison in this unlabelled remark is affected; Proposition adj_gengronwall and every result built on it (stab_thm, stab_cont, main_thm) are unchanged.
issues.title: False improvement factor 7^{1/beta} claimed for the adjusted Generalized Gronwall condition
issues.why_classification: The misstatement is self-contained in a remark; no theorem, hypothesis, or numerical result depends on it, and a one-line correction of the factor (or deleting the claim) fully resolves it with no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The extra term ℓ₁∫(ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰)∇c̃⁰·∇φ arising after adding and subtracting ρ̃¹ is bounded by splitting ∇c̃⁰ = ∇c_h⁰ + (∇c̃⁰−∇c_h⁰), which yields ℓ₁∫(ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰)∇c_h⁰·∇φ + ℓ₁‖ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰‖_{L^∞}‖c̃⁰−c_h⁰‖_{H¹} ≤ ℓ₁∫(ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰)∇c_h⁰·∇φ + ‖ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰‖_{L^∞}η_Ω⁰; cf. the plus sign in the analogous bound ‖ρ̃^{n+1}‖_{L^∞}η_Ω^n in conv-res. The lemma states the η_Ω⁰ term with a minus sign, so the stated upper bound is too small by 2‖ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰‖_{L^∞}η_Ω⁰ and the inequality does not follow; it is generically false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign to '+' in conv-res0 and include ‖ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰‖_{L^∞}η_Ω⁰ in the n=0 terms summed into Θ_{K,0} in main_thm; with this single correction all conclusions of main_thm hold with the slightly enlarged estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The n=0 time slab of the estimator in Theorem main_thm (defined by summing the bounds of Lemmas diff-res0, time-res0 and conv-res0) misses the positive contribution (‖ρ̃¹−ρ̃⁰‖_{L^∞}η_Ω⁰)², so the residual bound (estimator) and with it the error estimates in i) and ii) are not established as stated.
issues.title: Sign error in conv-res0: the eta_Omega^0 term must enter with a plus sign
issues.why_classification: The defect is a one-sign error in a residual lemma; the repair is a local sign flip plus adding one positive term to the first time slab's estimator, after which every theorem and guarantee survives unchanged. No new lemma, construction, or argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \int_\Omega c_h^n v_h + \nabla c_h^n \cdot \nabla v_h \ dx = \int_\Omega \rho_h^n v_h \ dx, \quad \forall v_h \in V_h,

issues.failure_explanation: The manufactured solutions satisfy c−Δc = ρ+g with g = (2π² + t/(1+t))cos(πx)cos(πy) ≠ 0 in 2D (and g = (1+6π²−1/(1+t))cos(2πx)cos(πy)cos(πz) ≠ 0 in 3D), and the parabolic equation with f ≠ 0, whereas Algorithm FV-FE-algo — via the homogeneous FE scheme (FE) and FV scheme — approximates the homogeneous Keller-Segel system. Hence the numerical solution produced by the stated algorithm converges to the homogeneous solution, not to the manufactured one, and the reported 'exact' errors in Table scaling cannot tend to zero as displayed. If a forced variant was in fact solved (as the steadily decreasing errors indicate), then the computed Θ_Ω is the discretization residual of the forced scheme and does not bound the residual R_{ρ̃} = ∂_tρ̃ + div(ρ̃∇c̃) − Δρ̃ that inequality (estimator) of Theorem main_thm bounds; the experiment therefore does not test the paper's estimator.

failure_location.quote: We compute the 'exact' error of the interpolation of Morley-type of the numerical approximations, computed using Algorithm \ref{FV-FE-algo}, to the manufactured solution above measured in the $L^\infty(0,T;L^2)$-norm and the $L^2(0,T;H^1)$-norm for different refinements of our mesh, as explained above.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the scaling experiment for the homogeneous problem (e.g., manufactured solutions with f = g = 0) or extend the scheme and the residual estimator to include the forcing terms f, g (adding them to the residual decomposition in (residual_sum) and to the estimator) and re-derive the corresponding bound; at minimum the mismatch between the forced test problem and the homogeneous algorithm and theorem must be resolved.
issues.overall_effect: The scaling test's conclusions — order-2 'exact' error, order-1 estimator, and the claim that the estimator 'converges optimally' — are not valid evidence for the homogeneous-system estimator and error control of Theorem main_thm. The formal theorems themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Manufactured solutions solve a forced system (f, g nonzero) inconsistent with the homogeneous FV-FE algorithm and the homogeneous-residual estimator
issues.why_classification: The formal results survive, but the numerical evidence for the estimator's convergence and optimality must be re-established either by a new experiment for the homogeneous system or by a nontrivial extension of the estimator to forced problems; this is a contained but non-routine repair of the numerical section with no loss to the theorems.
